problems.question: Each morning of her five-day workweek, Jane bought either a \(50\)-cent muffin or a \(75\)-cent bagel. Her total cost for the week was a whole number of dollars. How many bagels did she buy?
hints: With \(b\) bagels the total is \(50(5-b)+75b\) cents
A whole number of dollars means that total is a multiple of \(100\)
problems.solution: If Jane buys \(b\) bagels, she buys \(5-b\) muffins, for a total of \[ 50(5-b)+75b = 250+25b \] cents. This is a whole number of dollars when \(250+25b\) is a multiple of \(100,\) that is, when \(25b\equiv50\pmod{100},\) or \(b\equiv2\pmod4.\) The only value with \(0\le b\le5\) is \(b=2.\) Thus, the correct answer is B.

problems.question: Which of the following is equal to \[\dfrac{\frac13-\frac14\ }{\ \frac12-\frac13\ }?\]
hints: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(12\)
\(\dfrac13-\dfrac14=\dfrac1{12}\) and \(\dfrac12-\dfrac13=\dfrac16\)
problems.solution: The least common denominator of the small fractions is \(12,\) so multiply top and bottom by \(12:\) \[ \dfrac{\frac13-\frac14}{\frac12-\frac13}=\dfrac{4-3}{6-4}=\dfrac12. \] Thus, the correct answer is C.

problems.question: Paula the painter had just enough paint for \(30\) identically sized rooms. Unfortunately, on the way to work, three cans of paint fell off her truck, so she had only enough paint for \(25\) rooms. How many cans of paint did she use for the \(25\) rooms?
hints: Losing \(3\) cans cost her exactly \(5\) rooms
The paint-per-room rate is \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of a can
problems.solution: The lost \(3\) cans would have painted \(30-25=5\) rooms, so each room takes \(\dfrac35\) of a can. For \(25\) rooms she used \(\dfrac35\cdot25=15\) cans. Thus, the correct answer is C.

problems.question: A rectangular yard contains two flower beds in the shape of congruent isosceles right triangles. The remainder of the yard has a trapezoidal shape, as shown. The parallel sides of the trapezoid have lengths \(15\) and \(25\) meters. What fraction of the yard is occupied by the flower beds?
hints: Each triangle’s legs are half of \(25-15\)
Compare the total triangle area to the full rectangle of dimensions \(25\times5\)
problems.solution: The two parallel sides differ by \(25-15=10,\) split evenly between the two triangles, so each isosceles right triangle has legs of length \(5\) and area \(\dfrac12\cdot5^2=\dfrac{25}{2}.\) Together the beds cover \(25\) square meters. The rectangle has length \(25\) and width \(5,\) so area \(125.\) The fraction is \(\dfrac{25}{125}=\dfrac15.\) Thus, the correct answer is C.

problems.question: Twenty percent less than \(60\) is one-third more than what number?
hints: Twenty percent less than \(60\) is \(\dfrac45\cdot60\)
One-third more than \(n\) is \(\dfrac43 n\)
problems.solution: Twenty percent less than \(60\) is \(\dfrac45\cdot60=48.\) If \(n\) is the unknown number, one-third more than \(n\) is \(\dfrac43 n,\) so \[ \dfrac43 n=48 \]\[ n=36. \] Thus, the correct answer is D.

problems.question: Kiana has two older twin brothers. The product of their three ages is \(128.\) What is the sum of their three ages?
hints: Every age divides \(128=2^7,\) and the twins share one age
If the twins are \(t\) and Kiana is \(k,\) then \(t^2 k=128\) with \(k\lt t\)
problems.solution: Since \(128=2^7,\) every age is a power of \(2.\) Writing the twins’ common age as \(t\) and Kiana’s as \(k,\) we need \(t^2k=128\) with \(k\lt t.\) Write \(t=2^j.\) Then \(k=2^{7-2j}.\) For \(k\) to be a positive integer age we need \(7-2j\ge0,\) so \(j\le3.\) Because Kiana is younger than the twins, \(7-2j\lt j,\) so \(j\ge3.\) Therefore \(j=3,\) giving \(t=8\) and \(k=2.\) The sum is \(8+8+2=18.\) Thus, the correct answer is D.

problems.question: By inserting parentheses, it is possible to give the expression \[2\times3+4\times5\] several values. How many different values can be obtained?
hints: Decide which operation is performed last
Try groupings such as \((2\times3)+(4\times5)\) and \((2\times3+4)\times5\)
problems.solution: There are five full parenthesizations of four numbers joined by three operations. Evaluating all five gives \(((2\times3)+4)\times5=50\) and \((2\times(3+4))\times5=70.\) \((2\times3)+(4\times5)=26.\) \(2\times((3+4)\times5)=70\) and \(2\times(3+(4\times5))=46.\) Thus the distinct values are \(26, 46, 50,\) and \(70,\) for a total of \(4.\) Thus, the correct answer is C.

problems.question: In a certain year the price of gasoline rose by \(20\%\) during January, fell by \(20\%\) during February, rose by \(25\%\) during March, and fell by \(x\%\) during April. The price of gasoline at the end of April was the same as it had been at the beginning of January. To the nearest integer, what is \(x?\)
hints: After March the price is \((1.2)(0.8)(1.25)\) times the starting price
April must divide out a factor of \(1.2\)
problems.solution: Let \(p\) be the starting price. After March the price is \[ (1.2)(0.8)(1.25)p=1.2p. \] The April drop must return it to \(p,\) so it removes \(0.2p,\) a fraction \[ x=100\cdot\dfrac{0.2p}{1.2p}=\dfrac{100}{6}\approx16.7. \] To the nearest integer, \(x=17.\) Thus, the correct answer is B.

problems.question: Segment \(BD\) and \(AE\) intersect at \(C,\) as shown, \(AB=BC=CD=CE,\) and \(\angle A=\dfrac52\angle B.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle D?\)
hints: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB=BC\) so \(\angle A=\angle C\)
\(\angle DCE\) equals \(\angle ACB\) by vertical angles, and \(\triangle CDE\) is isosceles
problems.solution: Since \(\triangle ABC\) is isosceles with \(AB=BC,\) we have \(\angle A=\angle C.\) With \(\angle A=\dfrac52\angle B,\) the angle sum gives \[ \dfrac52\angle B+\dfrac52\angle B+\angle B=180^\circ, \] so \(\angle B=30^\circ\) and \(\angle ACB=75^\circ.\) By vertical angles \(\angle DCE=75^\circ.\) Since \(CD=CE,\) triangle \(CDE\) is isosceles, so \[ 2\angle D+75^\circ=180^\circ, \] giving \(\angle D=52.5^\circ.\) Thus, the correct answer is A.

problems.question: A flagpole is originally \(5\) meters tall. A hurricane snaps the flagpole at a point \(x\) meters above the ground so that the upper part, still attached to the stump, touches the ground \(1\) meter away from the base. What is \(x?\)
hints: The broken piece has length \(5-x\) and forms the hypotenuse
problems.solution: The standing stump has height \(x,\) and the snapped piece of length \(5-x\) is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs \(x\) and \(1.\) By the Pythagorean Theorem, \[ \begin{aligned} x^2+1^2 &= (5-x)^2 \\ &= x^2-10x+25, \end{aligned} \] so \(10x=24\) and \(x=2.4.\) Thus, the correct answer is E.

problems.question: How many \(7\)-digit palindromes (numbers that read the same backward as forward) can be formed using the digits \(2,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(5,\) \(5,\) \(5?\)
hints: In a \(7\)-digit palindrome the middle digit appears an odd number of times
The first three digits determine the last three; count their orderings
problems.solution: A \(7\)-digit palindrome has the form with the middle digit used once and the outer three digits each used twice. Only \(5\) appears an odd number of times, so \(5\) must be the middle digit. The remaining digits \(2,3,5\) fill the first three positions in some order and mirror to the last three. There are \(3!=6\) such orderings. Thus, the correct answer is A.

problems.question: Distinct points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) and \(D\) lie on a line, with \(AB=BC=CD=1.\) Points \(E\) and \(F\) lie on a second line, parallel to the first, with \(EF=1.\) A triangle with positive area has three of the six points as its vertices. How many possible values are there for the area of the triangle?
hints: The height is the fixed distance between the two parallel lines
Count the distinct base lengths available on either line
problems.solution: A positive-area triangle uses two points on one line as its base and one point on the other line as its apex. The height is always the fixed distance between the lines, so the area depends only on the base length. Bases on the first line can be \(1, 2,\) or \(3;\) a base on the second line is \(1.\) So the distinct base lengths are \(1, 2, 3,\) giving three possible areas. Thus, the correct answer is A.

problems.question: As shown below, convex pentagon \(ABCDE\) has sides \(AB=3,\) \(BC=4,\) \(CD=6,\) \(DE=3,\) and \(EA=7.\) The pentagon is originally positioned in the plane with vertex \(A\) at the origin and vertex \(B\) on the positive \(x\)-axis. The pentagon is then rolled clockwise to the right along the \(x\)-axis. Which side will touch the point \(x=2009\) on the \(x\)-axis?
hints: The perimeter is \(23,\) and \(2009=23\cdot87+8\)
After \(87\) full turns, track where vertices \(A, B, C, D\) land
problems.solution: The pentagon has perimeter \(3+4+6+3+7=23.\) One full roll advances the contact point by \(23,\) and \(2009=23\cdot87+8.\) After \(87\) rolls, vertex \(A\) sits at \(x=23\cdot87=2001\) and \(B\) at \(2004.\) Rolling further, \(C\) touches at \(2004+4=2008\) and \(D\) at \(2008+6=2014.\) Since \(2009\) lies between \(2008\) and \(2014,\) side \(\overline{CD}\) touches that point. Thus, the correct answer is C.

problems.question: On Monday, Millie puts a quart of seeds, \(25\%\) of which are millet, into a bird feeder. On each successive day she adds another quart of the same mix of seeds without removing any seeds that are left. Each day the birds eat only \(25\%\) of the millet in the feeder, but they eat all of the other seeds. On which day, just after Millie has placed the seeds, will the birds find that more than half the seeds in the feeder are millet?
hints: Each day the standing millet is multiplied by \(\dfrac34,\) then \(\dfrac14\) quart is added
Other seeds always total \(\dfrac34\) quart; find when millet first exceeds that
problems.solution: Each quart adds \(\dfrac14\) quart of millet, and the birds leave \(\dfrac34\) of the standing millet. On day \(n\) the millet present is \[ \begin{gathered} \dfrac14\left(1+\dfrac34+\cdots+\Big(\dfrac34\Big)^{n-1}\right) \\ = 1-\Big(\dfrac34\Big)^{n}. \end{gathered} \] The other seeds always total \(\dfrac34\) quart. Millet exceeds half when \(1-\Big(\dfrac34\Big)^n\gt\dfrac34,\) i.e. \(\Big(\dfrac34\Big)^n\lt\dfrac14.\) Since \(\Big(\dfrac34\Big)^4=\dfrac{81}{256}\gt\dfrac14\) but \(\Big(\dfrac34\Big)^5=\dfrac{243}{1024}\lt\dfrac14,\) this first happens on day \(5,\) which is Friday. Thus, the correct answer is D.

problems.question: When a bucket is two-thirds full of water, the bucket and water weigh \(a\) kilograms. When the bucket is one-half full of water the total weight is \(b\) kilograms. In terms of \(a\) and \(b,\) what is the total weight in kilograms when the bucket is full of water?
hints: Let \(x\) be the empty bucket’s weight and \(y\) a full load of water
Subtract \(x+\dfrac12 y=b\) from \(x+\dfrac23 y=a\) to find \(y\)
problems.solution: Let \(x\) be the bucket’s weight and \(y\) the weight of a full load of water. Then \[x+\dfrac23 y=a\] and \[x+\dfrac12 y=b.\] Subtracting gives \(\dfrac16 y=a-b,\) so \(y=6a-6b,\) and \(x=b-\dfrac12 y=4b-3a.\) The full bucket weighs \[ \begin{aligned} x+y &= (4b-3a)+(6a-6b) \\ &= 3a-2b. \end{aligned} \] Thus, the correct answer is E.

problems.question: Points \(A\) and \(C\) lie on a circle centered at \(O,\) each of \(\overline{BA}\) and \(\overline{BC}\) are tangent to the circle, and \(\triangle ABC\) is equilateral. The circle intersects \(\overline{BO}\) at \(D.\) What is \(\dfrac{BD}{BO}?\)
hints: Equilateral \(\triangle ABC\) gives \(\angle OBC=30^\circ,\) and \(OC\perp BC\)
In a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle the hypotenuse \(BO=2\,OC\)
problems.solution: Let the radius be \(r.\) By symmetry \(BO\) bisects the \(60^\circ\) angle \(ABC,\) so \(\angle OBC=30^\circ.\) Since \(OC\perp BC,\) triangle \(BCO\) is a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle with hypotenuse \(BO=2\,OC=2r.\) Then \(BD=BO-OD=2r-r=r,\) so \(\dfrac{BD}{BO}=\dfrac{r}{2r}=\dfrac12.\) Thus, the correct answer is B.

problems.question: Five unit squares are arranged in the coordinate plane as shown, with the lower left corner at the origin. The slanted line, extending from \((a,0)\) to \((3,3),\) divides the entire region into two regions of equal area. What is \(a?\)
hints: The whole region has area \(5,\) so each part must be \(\dfrac52\)
The lower-right part is a triangle of base \(3-a\) and height \(3,\) with one unit square removed
problems.solution: The five unit squares have total area \(5,\) so each region must have area \(\dfrac52.\) The region to the lower right of the line is a right triangle with legs \(3-a\) and \(3,\) minus the one unit square it does not cover. Setting its area to \(\dfrac52\) gives \[ \dfrac{3(3-a)}{2}-1=\dfrac52, \] so \(3(3-a)=7\) and \(a=\dfrac23.\) Thus, the correct answer is C.

problems.question: Rectangle \(ABCD\) has \(AB=8\) and \(BC=6.\) Point \(M\) is the midpoint of diagonal \(\overline{AC},\) and \(E\) is on \(\overline{AB}\) with \(\overline{ME}\perp\overline{AC}.\) What is the area of \(\triangle AME?\)
hints: \(\triangle AME\sim\triangle ABC,\) giving \(\dfrac{ME}{AM}=\dfrac{BC}{AB}\)
problems.solution: By the Pythagorean Theorem, \(AC=\sqrt{8^2+6^2}=10,\) so \(AM=5.\) Right triangles \(AME\) and \(ABC\) share angle \(A,\) so they are similar with \[ \dfrac{ME}{AM}=\dfrac{BC}{AB}=\dfrac68, \] giving \(ME=\dfrac{15}{4}.\) Then \[ \begin{gathered} [\triangle AME]=\dfrac12\cdot AM\cdot ME \\ = \dfrac12\cdot5\cdot\dfrac{15}{4}=\dfrac{75}{8}. \end{gathered} \] Thus, the correct answer is D.

problems.question: A particular \(12\)-hour digital clock displays the hour and minute of a day. Unfortunately, whenever it is supposed to display a \(1,\) it mistakenly displays a \(9.\) For example, when it is \(1{:}16\) PM the clock incorrectly shows \(9{:}96\) PM. What fraction of the day will the clock show the correct time?
hints: The hour is wrong only for \(1,\) \(10,\) \(11,\) \(12\)
A minute is wrong when either of its digits is a \(1;\) count those out of \(60\)
problems.solution: Among the hours \(1\) through \(12,\) exactly \(1,\) \(10,\) \(11,\) \(12\) contain a \(1,\) so the hour is correct \(\dfrac{8}{12}=\dfrac23\) of the time. A minute is displayed wrong when its tens digit is \(1\) (minutes \(10\)–\(19\)) or its units digit is \(1\) (\(01,11,\dots,51\)), which is \(15\) of the \(60\) minutes. So the minute is correct \(\dfrac{45}{60}=\dfrac34\) of the time. The clock is correct \(\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac34=\dfrac12\) of the day. Thus, the correct answer is A.

problems.question: Triangle \(ABC\) has a right angle at \(B,\) \(AB=1,\) and \(BC=2.\) The bisector of \(\angle BAC\) meets \(\overline{BC}\) at \(D.\) What is \(BD?\)
hints: By the Angle Bisector Theorem, \(\dfrac{BD}{DC}=\dfrac{AB}{AC}\)
\(AC=\sqrt5\) and \(BD+DC=2\)
problems.solution: By the Pythagorean Theorem, \(AC=\sqrt{1^2+2^2}=\sqrt5.\) The Angle Bisector Theorem gives \[ \dfrac{BD}{DC}=\dfrac{AB}{AC}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}, \] so \(DC=\sqrt5\,BD.\) Since \(BD+DC=2,\) we have \(BD(1+\sqrt5)=2,\) so \[ BD=\dfrac{2}{1+\sqrt5}=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{2}. \] Thus, the correct answer is B.

problems.question: What is the remainder when \[3^0+3^1+3^2+\cdots+3^{2009}\] is divided by \(8?\)
hints: Group the \(2010\) terms into blocks of four and handle the leftover
problems.solution: Any four consecutive powers of \(3\) sum to a multiple of \(3^0+3^1+3^2+3^3=40,\) which is divisible by \(8.\) The terms from \(3^2\) to \(3^{2009}\) split into such blocks and contribute remainder \(0.\) What remains is \(3^0+3^1=4.\) Thus, the correct answer is D.

problems.question: A cubical cake with edge length \(2\) inches is iced on the sides and the top. It is cut vertically into three pieces as shown in this top view, where \(M\) is the midpoint of a top edge. The piece whose top is triangle \(B\) contains \(c\) cubic inches of cake and \(s\) square inches of icing. What is \(c+s?\)
hints: Triangle \(B\) is similar to the triangle whose legs are \(1\) and \(2\)
The icing on \(B\) covers its top face and the entire cube face it borders
problems.solution: Set the top face as a \(2\times2\) square. The cut from \(M\) toward the far corner creates the top triangle \(A\) with legs \(1\) and \(2,\) so area \(1\) and hypotenuse \(\sqrt5.\) Triangle \(B\) is similar to \(A\) but with hypotenuse \(2,\) so its area is \(\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}\right)^2\cdot1=\dfrac45.\) Since the cake has height \(2,\) the volume is \(c=\dfrac45\cdot2=\dfrac85.\) The icing on this piece is its top (\(\dfrac45\)) plus the full cube side face it borders (\(2\times2=4\)), so \(s=\dfrac45+4=\dfrac{24}{5}.\) Therefore \(c+s=\dfrac85+\dfrac{24}{5}=\dfrac{32}{5}.\) Thus, the correct answer is B.

problems.question: Rachel and Robert run on a circular track. Rachel runs counterclockwise and completes a lap every \(90\) seconds, and Robert runs clockwise and completes a lap every \(80\) seconds. Both start from the start line at the same time. At some random time between \(10\) minutes and \(11\) minutes after they begin to run, a photographer standing inside the track takes a picture that shows one-fourth of the track, centered on the starting line. What is the probability that both Rachel and Robert are in the picture?
hints: The picture covers \(\dfrac18\) of a lap on each side of the start line
Find each runner’s window of time inside that region during the \(10\)th minute, then overlap them
problems.solution: The picture spans \(\dfrac18\) lap on each side of the start. After \(600\) seconds Rachel is \(30\) seconds short of the line; running \(\dfrac14\) lap in \(22.5\) seconds, she is in view between \(30-11.25=18.75\) and \(30+11.25=41.25\) seconds of the \(10\)th minute. After \(600\) seconds Robert is \(40\) seconds from the line; running \(\dfrac14\) lap in \(20\) seconds, he is in view between \(30\) and \(50\) seconds. Both appear between \(30\) and \(41.25\) seconds, a window of length \(11.25\) out of \(60,\) so the probability is \(\dfrac{11.25}{60}=\dfrac{3}{16}.\) Thus, the correct answer is C.

problems.question: The keystone arch is an ancient architectural feature. It is composed of congruent isosceles trapezoids fitted together along the non-parallel sides, as shown. The bottom sides of the two end trapezoids are horizontal. In an arch made with \(9\) trapezoids, let \(x\) be the angle measure in degrees of the larger interior angle of the trapezoid. What is \(x?\)
hints: Reflect the arch to close it into a full loop of \(18\) trapezoids
The inner vertices form a regular \(18\)-gon; use its interior angle
problems.solution: Adding a mirror image completes the arch into a symmetric closed loop of \(18\) trapezoids. Their inner edges form a regular \(18\)-gon, each interior angle of which is \[ \dfrac{(18-2)\cdot180^\circ}{18}=160^\circ. \] At each inner vertex, two of the trapezoids’ larger angles \(x\) meet the \(160^\circ\) angle around a full turn: \(x+x+160^\circ=360^\circ,\) so \(x=100.\) Thus, the correct answer is A.

problems.question: Each face of a cube is given a single narrow stripe painted from the center of one edge to the center of its opposite edge. The choice of the edge pairing is made at random and independently for each face. What is the probability that there is a continuous stripe encircling the cube?
hints: Each face has \(2\) equally likely stripe orientations, so \(2^6\) total configurations
There are \(3\) possible encircling bands, each fixing the orientation of \(4\) faces
problems.solution: Each face’s stripe has \(2\) orientations, giving \(2^6=64\) equally likely configurations. An encircling stripe runs around one of the \(3\) pairs of opposite faces. For a given band, the \(4\) faces it crosses must each be oriented to continue it, a probability of \(\left(\dfrac12\right)^4=\dfrac{1}{16}.\) The three bands are mutually exclusive, so the probability is \(3\cdot\dfrac{1}{16}=\dfrac{3}{16}.\) Thus, the correct answer is B.
